Keywords: layer caching, dockerfile order, build cache, cache invalidation
Guidance: Copying the entire source tree before installing dependencies busts the Docker build cache on every code change, forcing a full dependency reinstall each build.
Do: Copy dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt) and install first, then copy the rest of the source.
Don't: COPY . . before installing dependencies in a Dockerfile.

Keywords: multi-stage build, build stage, final image size
Guidance: Shipping build tools (compilers, dev headers) in the final production image bloats it and expands the attack surface unnecessarily.
Do: Use multi-stage builds: compile/build in one stage, copy only the compiled artifact into a minimal final stage.
Don't: Ship the same image used to compile the app as the production runtime image.
Example:
FROM golang:1.22 AS build
RUN go build -o app
FROM gcr.io/distroless/base
COPY --from=build /app /app

Keywords: non-root user, USER directive, container privilege, root container
Guidance: Containers running as root by default mean a container-escape vulnerability hands the attacker root on the host (or at minimum root within the container's namespace).
Do: Add a USER directive with a non-root UID in every Dockerfile, and set runAsNonRoot at the orchestrator level too.
Don't: Leave the default root user active in production container images.

Keywords: dockerignore, build context, secrets in image, .git
Guidance: Without a .dockerignore, the entire build context -- including .git, local .env files, and node_modules -- gets sent to the daemon and can end up baked into layers.
Do: Maintain a .dockerignore excluding .git, .env, node_modules, and other local-only artifacts.
Don't: Build with no .dockerignore and let secrets/local files leak into the build context.

Keywords: docker-compose network, bridge network, service discovery
Guidance: Putting every service on the default bridge network with no explicit network segmentation means a compromised frontend container can reach the database container directly.
Do: Define explicit named networks in docker-compose and only attach services that genuinely need to talk to each other.
Don't: Leave all services on the default network with no segmentation between tiers.

Keywords: healthcheck, docker healthcheck, container restart, orchestrator readiness
Guidance: Without a HEALTHCHECK, Docker/orchestrators only know if the process is running, not if it's actually serving traffic -- a hung-but-alive process looks healthy forever.
Do: Define a HEALTHCHECK instruction (or compose healthcheck) that hits a real readiness endpoint.
Don't: Rely on 'container is running' as a proxy for 'container is healthy'.

Keywords: docker secrets, build args, env vars, image layers
Guidance: Passing secrets via ENV or ARG gets them baked into image layers and visible via docker history, even if a later layer 'deletes' the file.
Do: Use BuildKit secret mounts (--secret) or runtime secret injection, never ENV/ARG, for credentials.
Don't: Pass an API key via --build-arg and bake it into an image layer.

Keywords: base image tag, image digest, latest tag, supply chain
Guidance: Building FROM a mutable tag like node:latest means the same Dockerfile can produce a different image next week with no code change, breaking reproducibility and supply-chain guarantees.
Do: Pin base images to a specific version tag or digest (FROM node:20.11-slim@sha256:...).

Keywords: buildkit, cache mount, docker build, dependency cache
Guidance: Without BuildKit's cache mounts, package manager caches (apt, pip, npm) get re-downloaded on every build even when layer caching itself is invalidated for unrelated reasons.
Do: Enable BuildKit and use --mount=type=cache for package manager directories to persist download caches across builds.
Don't: Build without BuildKit cache mounts and re-download all dependencies on every cache miss.

Keywords: image size, alpine, distroless, slim image
Guidance: Using a full OS base image (ubuntu, debian) for a runtime that only needs a language runtime bloats images to hundreds of MB, slowing pulls and expanding attack surface.
Do: Prefer slim/alpine/distroless base images for the final stage when compatible with your runtime's libc requirements.
Don't: Default to the full ubuntu/debian base image for every container.

Keywords: docker-compose, environment variables, .env file, dev prod parity
Guidance: Hardcoding different config directly into multiple docker-compose.override files per environment drifts silently; a single .env-driven compose file is easier to keep consistent.
Do: Drive environment differences through .env files and variable substitution in a single docker-compose.yml.
Don't: Maintain separate full docker-compose.yml copies per environment that duplicate 90% of the config.

Guidance: No restart policy means a crashed container stays dead until someone notices and manually restarts it, turning a transient failure into an outage.
Do: Set restart: unless-stopped (or on-failure with a max retry count) for long-running services.
Don't: Leave restart policy unset ("no") on production services.

Keywords: docker scan, trivy, image scanning, cve
Guidance: Pushing images to a registry without scanning them means known CVEs in base images or dependencies ship straight to production undetected.
Do: Scan images in CI with a tool like Trivy or Docker Scout before pushing to the registry, and fail the build on critical CVEs.
Don't: Push images to production registries with no vulnerability scan gate in CI.

Topic: Layer count and RUN instruction consolidation
Keywords: run instruction, layer count, image bloat, apt-get clean
Guidance: Each RUN instruction creates a new layer; leftover apt cache from an unconsolidated RUN apt-get install (without cleanup in the same layer) stays in the image even if a later layer deletes it.
Do: Chain related RUN commands (install, cleanup) in a single instruction so intermediate layers don't retain deleted files.
Don't: Run apt-get install in one RUN and rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* in a separate later RUN.
Example: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
